arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Utah's lawyer argued the arrest was lawful and independent.
Strieff's lawyer argued the unlawful stop caused the warrant discovery.
Justice Sotomayor asked what was objectively reasonable about the stop.
Justice Kagan questioned the likelihood of finding a warrant during a stop.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Police stopped Strieff without reasonable suspicion. They found an arrest warrant. They searched him and found drugs. The lower court suppressed the drugs. Utah wants the Court to admit the evidence.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the scope of the exclusionary rule. It determines whether police can use unlawful stops to find warrants. It affects how courts handle evidence from flawed police conduct.
